name: AOBP Integration
description: Records an AOBP blood pressure measurement from a Uscom BP+ device directly into a REDCap survey, using the BP+ JavaScript SDK.
$comment-logging: A capability, not a policy. From framework version 11 the framework
refuses log() from an unauthenticated context unless this is set. This
module renders on the survey page and nowhere else, so that is every call
it makes -- unset, it has no account of itself at all, and an empty log is
not evidence that nothing went wrong.
It cannot be changed from the Control Center or a project: the framework
reads it from the installed version's config.json.
Nothing a caller wrote reaches the log. Every value is either a literal
in the module or a context parameter the framework supplies, which the
hook documentation says can be trusted when set.

authors.name: Oliver Stanesby
authors.institution: Menzies Institute for Medical Research, University of Tasmania

project-settings.name:
Instrument that carries the AOBP controls
The unique instrument name, not its label. Blank uses aobp_visit.

Instrument that uses the collapsible information panels
The unique instrument name, not its label. Blank uses info. This is the participant-facing information form, not the one that carries the AOBP controls.

Set the device clock from this computer when it is out by more than this many minutes
The device time stamps measurements. The device clock does not track daylight savings changes. Enabling the check ensures the device clock is aligned with the survey host clock. Blank defaults to 5 minutes.

Show warnings from attempts the device recovered from
The BP+ may automatically retry a measurement and include an alert in the xml result. A retry may subsequently succeed. Turn ON if you want to see the warnings on measurements that succeeded after the retry. The alerts are recorded in the XML even when not displayed.

Store the raw measurement XML as a file on the record
A full xml result file can exceed the maximum size (65,000) permitted in a text field. Enable to save the full xml result in File Upload fields named seated_raw_xml and standing_raw_xml.

What to send the device as the patient ID
The device writes this verbatim into the xml result file which is saved to the SD card (when one is fitted). The patient ID may be useful to reconcile a card full of recordings back to REDCap records. Note a card is removable and nothing on it is access-controlled.

choices.name: The record ID on its own
Nothing -- the device stores no patient ID

project-settings.name:
Custom Patient ID template
Used when 'Custom Patient ID template' is selected above. [record], [instance] and [position] are replaced; everything else is sent as typed. Add :5 to pad record or instance with leading zeros to the specified number of digits. e.g. [record:5] to pad result to 5 digits. [position] is the seated or standing if needed. AOBP results already record bodyPosition in the XML.

Log every serial line to the browser console
Troubleshooting only. Every command sent to the BP+ and every line it answers with, which is what a support report needs when a device behaves differently on one site and not another. Off for normal use: it says nothing an operator can act on.

TESTING ONLY — simulated BP+
When enabled, the survey, the file storage and the record can be tested with no BP+ and no cable using measurements from a built-in simulator instead of a real device. Readings are fabricated. The page displays a warning in a red banner, and every record is written with a device id beginning SIMULATED-. Never enable this on a project collecting real data.
